blocks.content: Rocks inside the Earth are constantly subjected to forces generated by plate movements. These forces create stress, which leads to deformation known as strain.
Within the elastic limit, stress is directly proportional to strain.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Stress is the internal restoring force developed per unit area inside a deformed body.
Strain is defined as the ratio of change in dimension to the original dimension and is a dimensionless quantity.
Hooke's Law states that within the elastic limit, stress is directly proportional to strain.
Modulus of Elasticity depends on the material's nature and temperature, remaining independent of body geometry.
Steel is physically more elastic than rubber because steel requires a larger force to produce the same strain.
Breaking stress depends solely on the nature of the material, independent of the wire's length or cross-sectional area.
Strain energy per unit volume in a stretched wire is calculated as 1/2 × stress × strain.
Poisson's ratio theoretically ranges from -1 to 0.5, but practical values for real materials lie between 0 and 0.5.

cells: Forces rocks to slide past each other

blocks.content: When stress remains below the elastic limit, rocks bend but return to their original shape. When the elastic limit is exceeded, rocks fracture suddenly — producing an earthquake.
